body.cap: Bandora CEO Marcia Pereira (middle) stood with CTA CEO Gary Shapiro (left) and CTA President Kinsey Fabrizio (right) for the commemorative photo after the CTA CEO Summit startup pitch competition | Photo courtesy of UPTEC

body.x: The Lisbon competition featured five startups across sectors such as health, energy, AI, and entertainment, pitching to a panel of prominent investors. Bandora’s solution integrates seamlessly into existing IoT systems to continuously optimize energy management. Since its founding in 2017, the company has optimized more than 16,500 m² of buildings, reducing carbon emissions by 215 tons of CO₂ by the end of 2023.

“Tech innovation can solve big global challenges and improve millions of lives, and these startups are shaping the future,” said Gary Shapiro, CEO and Vice Chair of CTA. “We’re thrilled to welcome Bandora to Eureka Park. There is nowhere better for innovative startups to meet global investors, partners, and media.”
The judging panel included Rita Branco of 3xP Global Investments, Cintia Mano of COREangels, Tomás Penaguião of Bynd Venture Capital, João Pereira of Portugal Ventures, and Diogo Teixeira of Beta-i.

“Winning the CEO Summit pitch competition in front of such an inspiring group of innovators and investors is an honor,” said Marcia Pereira, Founder and CEO of Bandora. “Exhibiting in Eureka Park at CES 2026 is an incredible opportunity for us to share our vision, meet investors, and grow our global connections to expand internationally.”

Eureka Park, known as the launchpad for groundbreaking startups, will host 1,400 companies at CES 2026, running from January 6 to 9 in Las Vegas. The Lisbon pitch competition is part of CTA’s broader effort to spotlight Europe’s innovation ecosystem, with momentum continuing at CES Unveiled Europe in Amsterdam on October 28, 2025.
